newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan copper cable shipments seen flat in 1997/98.
newsitem.headline: Japan copper cable shipments seen flat in 1997/98.

text.p: Japanese copper wire and cable shipments are expected to be flat in the fiscal year beginning April 1 compared with the current fiscal year, the Japanese Electric Wire and Cable Makers' Association said on Wednesday.
Shipments in 1996/97 were projected to rise 1.9 percent to 1,050,600 tonnes, the first increase in six years, followed by a marginal rise of 0.1 percent in 1997/98 to 1,052,000 tonnes.

The association's 1997/98 estimate was based on a forecast rise in Japan's gross domestic product of 1.5 percent, below the government's forecast of 1.9 percent, reflecting the industry's pessimism about the likely impact of this April's national sales tax hike, an association official said.
On the other hand, factors likely to bolster demand next year included low interest rates, government deregulation and robust spending on plant and equipment, he said.

The association predicted that shipments in the first half of 1997/98 would fall 3.9 percent from the prior half-year to 517,000 tonnes, but would then grow 3.5 percent in the second half to 535,000 tonnes.
